subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Which fixed-overhead reductions should OpenClaw pursue in core next, and should lazy/slim schema behavior remain opt-in through Tool Search/config or become a broader default?
rationale: The remaining work crosses prompt policy, provider-visible schemas, message-channel compatibility, plugin/declarative tools, and config/default behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary.

options.title: Sequence Incremental Core Reductions
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and land measured slices such as duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool-list suppression, compatibility-aware message pruning, cron description trimming, and Tool Search/deferred-schema hardening.

options.title: Delegate To Narrow Trackers
options.body: Let the open narrower issues own their specific slices and keep this issue as background only, accepting that cross-cutting progress may be fragmented.

options.title: Freeze New Schema Modes
options.body: Keep existing Tool Search, local lean mode, and allow/deny controls as the only supported token controls until maintainers revisit the broader prompt-budget roadmap.

recommendation.title: Sequence Incremental Core Reductions
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and land measured slices such as duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool-list suppression, compatibility-aware message pruning, cron description trimming, and Tool Search/deferred-schema hardening.
